The Opacity Loss is a regularization term used in differentiable volume rendering to enforce geometric consistency when a binary object mask is available [S1].

The claim states that the Opacity Loss is a regularization term used in differentiable volume rendering to enforce geometric consistency when a binary object mask is available. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly defines an 'Object Mask Constraint' using a binary cross entropy loss ($L_O$) when an object mask is available. It states that this constraint forces the rendered opacity ($O$) to align with the mask distribution ($M$), resulting in an 'opaque surface'. In the context of differentiable volume rendering (specifically Gaussian Splatting as implied by the notation $T_i, alpha_i$), enforcing an opaque surface via opacity alignment with a mask is a standard method for ensuring geometric consistency (preventing floating artifacts and defining the object boundary). Therefore, the evidence supports the claim that this loss is used to enforce geometric consistency (via surface definition) when a mask is available.
